graft.title: Encryption at rest on sylva's crypt: drop alfred-core's copy of the cipher
graft.need: crates/alfred-core/src/crypto.rs is a second copy of what sylva ships as the `crypt` feature (sylva::log::crypt, published in sylva 0.1.0): MasterKey (generate, from_hex, to_hex, derive), and a Cipher keyed by HMAC-SHA256(master, "<app>/v1/data") with XChaCha20-Poly1305 seal/open taking associated data, plus seal_text/open_text and the `e1:` + base64(nonce || ciphertext) form, byte for byte alfred's (so stored data needs no conversion). Use it: turn on sylva's `crypt` feature, build the cipher with `Cipher::new(&key, "alfred")`, and delete the copy. One thing sylva doesn't have is Cipher::blob_name: keep it in alfred on top of sylva's public `MasterKey::derive("alfred/v1/names")`, since blob naming is alfred's. For the op log, sylva::log::crypt::Encrypted is the sqlite ChainLog codec, if the store goes through sylva's ChainLog.
graft.use_case: One implementation of encryption at rest for every project that stores a log (the workspace principle: every capability has one owner). Fixes and reviews then happen once, in sylva, and alfred's store stays readable by anything that reads sylva's format.

answer.text: Done in 74c8d34 (not pushed yet): alfred-core turns on sylva's `crypt` and uses it. MasterKey is sylva's; Cipher wraps sylva's Cipher::new(key, "alfred") and keeps only blob_name, over MasterKey::derive("alfred/v1/names"); the op log goes through sylva::log::crypt::Encrypted, and the in-place encrypt/decrypt migrations use seal_text and open_payload. chacha20poly1305 is now only a dev-dependency, for a test that opens a payload sealed by the old derivation and checks blob names, so no store needs converting. Clippy -D warnings is clean and every test passes (alfred-core 114, alfred-server 36).
